title: Market Gardeners and Crop Growers
exposure_rationale: India's market-oriented cultivators are overwhelmingly self-employed small farmers doing physical field work. AI advisory tools for weather, pest identification, soil health and crop prices can help with decisions at the margins, but planting, tending and harvesting remain manual.

title: Mining and Construction Labourers
exposure_rationale: Mining and construction labourers carry, dig and load materials on sites, almost all as casual labour. The work is entirely physical and unaffected by AI.

title: Agricultural, Forestry and Fishery Labourers
exposure_rationale: Agricultural, forestry and fishery labourers, 95% casual wage workers in India, do manual field and farm work. AI has essentially no impact on their daily work.

title: Shop Salespersons
exposure_rationale: Most Indian shop salespersons are self-employed kirana and small-shop owners who serve customers in person, handle stock and extend credit to known buyers. AI may help with inventory, ordering and pricing, and e-commerce competition presses on the sector, but the face-to-face selling and shopkeeping core remains.

title: Animal Producers
exposure_rationale: Livestock, dairy and poultry producers in India are nearly all self-employed with low formal education, and their work is daily hands-on animal care. AI may offer veterinary or feed advice via phone apps, but it barely touches the core work.

title: Mixed Crop and Animal Workers
exposure_rationale: Mixed crop-and-animal farmers do physical field and livestock work, almost entirely as self-employed household enterprises. AI advisory services are peripheral at most.

title: Car, Van and Motorcycle Drivers
exposure_rationale: Car, taxi, auto and motorcycle drivers, two-thirds self-employed in India, spend their working time driving in highly unstructured traffic. AI already shapes dispatch and routing on ride-hailing apps, but autonomous driving is far from replacing drivers on Indian roads.

title: Subsistence Crop Farmers
exposure_rationale: Subsistence crop farmers grow food mainly for their own households with very low education and almost no market or digital interface. AI has essentially no effect on their daily work beyond occasional advisory information.

title: Garment and Related Trades Workers
exposure_rationale: Tailors, embroiderers, shoemakers and upholsterers in India are mostly self-employed and work by hand or on sewing machines. AI-driven pattern making and design affect a small number of pattern makers, but the core sewing and stitching is untouched.

title: Manufacturing Labourers
exposure_rationale: Hand packers and manufacturing labourers perform manual loading, packing and helper tasks in factories and brick kilns. Automation may reduce some packing jobs, but AI itself touches little of this physical work.

title: Building Frames and Related Trades Workers
exposure_rationale: Masons, bricklayers, stonecutters, concrete workers and carpenters do heavy manual work on construction sites, about half as casual labourers in India. AI has essentially no impact on the core tasks.

title: Domestic, Hotel and Office Cleaners and Helpers
exposure_rationale: Domestic, hotel and office cleaners and helpers do manual cleaning and household chores, a large share employed directly by Indian households. AI has essentially no impact on this work.

title: Managing Directors and Chief Executives
exposure_rationale: In India this group is mostly owner-proprietors (95% self-employed) running shops, wholesale businesses and eateries, not corporate CEOs. Their day is physical presence, supplier and customer dealings and cash management; AI can help with accounts, pricing and digital marketing, but the core of running a small physical business remains human.

title: Street and Market Salespersons
exposure_rationale: Street and market vendors in India are almost all self-employed, selling from stalls and preparing street food in person. Digital payments and phone ordering touch the margins, but haggling, handling goods and cooking on the street are physical and essentially unaffected by AI.

title: Handicraft Workers
exposure_rationale: Handicraft workers such as jewellers, potters, weavers, embroiderers, woodcarvers and sign painters produce goods by hand, mostly as self-employed artisans in India. AI can generate designs and patterns and support online selling, but the craft production itself remains manual.

title: Heavy Truck and Bus Drivers
exposure_rationale: Bus and truck drivers operate heavy vehicles on Indian roads and handle loading, passengers and vehicle care. AI helps with route planning and fleet management, but the driving itself remains a physical, real-time task with no near-term automation in India.

title: Cooks
exposure_rationale: Cooking in homes, dhabas, hotels and institutional kitchens is manual, real-time physical work. Two thirds of Indian cooks are salaried but almost all informally, many in households; AI may help with menu planning or recipes but does not touch the core job.

title: Food Processing and Related Trade Workers
exposure_rationale: Butchers, bakers, dairy makers, food preservers and bidi rollers (tobacco products is the top industry) do manual food and tobacco processing, mostly as self-employed home or small-unit workers in India. AI has little effect on these tasks.

title: Protective Service Workers
exposure_rationale: Security guards, watchmen, police constables, fire-fighters and prison guards protect people and property through physical presence and patrolling. AI-enabled CCTV analytics and digital reporting may reduce some monitoring headcount, but responding to incidents and maintaining order in person remain the core of the job.

title: Primary School and Early Childhood Teachers
exposure_rationale: Primary and pre-primary teachers spend much of their day on in-person care, supervision and foundational instruction for young children, often in rural government schools. AI can help with lesson plans, worksheets and record-keeping, but young children need a physically present adult, which limits exposure.

title: Machinery Mechanics and Repairers
exposure_rationale: Motor vehicle, machinery, aircraft and bicycle mechanics diagnose and repair equipment by hand, often in small self-run workshops in India. AI diagnostic tools can speed fault-finding, but the repair work itself is physical.

title: Transport and Storage Labourers
exposure_rationale: Rickshaw pullers, cart drivers, freight handlers, loaders and shelf fillers move goods and people by hand. AI-driven warehouse management may change how work is assigned, but the work itself is physical.

title: Painters, Builders, Structure Cleaners and Related Trades Workers
exposure_rationale: Building painters, spray painters and structure cleaners do manual work on site, mostly as casual labour in India. AI does not touch the core tasks.

title: Electrical Equipment Installers and Repairers
exposure_rationale: Electricians, electrical fitters and line installers do hands-on installation and repair work in buildings and on networks. AI may help with diagnostics, estimates and paperwork, but the core work requires physical presence and manual skill.

title: Other Sales Workers
exposure_rationale: This catch-all mixes call-centre and telesales staff, customer-care executives and collections agents, whose voice and chat work is highly exposed to AI agents, with door-to-door salespeople, petrol pump attendants, delivery workers, counter attendants and models whose work is physical. The average is moderate, but the contact-centre segment faces major restructuring.

title: Subsistence Livestock Farmers
exposure_rationale: Subsistence livestock keepers tend animals for household needs, with median education below primary. The work is entirely physical and AI has no meaningful impact on it.

title: Building Finishers and Related Trades Workers
exposure_rationale: Roofers, tile setters, plasterers, glaziers, plumbers and AC mechanics perform skilled hands-on work in buildings, much of it casual and informal in India. AI might help with troubleshooting or estimates for plumbers and AC mechanics, but the core work is physical.

title: Secondary Education Teachers
exposure_rationale: Secondary teachers prepare lessons, explain concepts, set and grade exams, and manage classrooms. AI can generate material, grade and tutor, but Indian classrooms (more than half in government schools) rely on in-person instruction, discipline and student care, so the human role remains central.

title: General Office Clerks
exposure_rationale: General office clerks process files, prepare documents, maintain records and handle correspondence following set procedures, which is routine information processing. In India many work in government offices and banks still moving from paper to digital, which may slow adoption, but the work itself is highly automatable.

title: Software and Application Developers, and Analysts
exposure_rationale: Software developers and analysts work entirely on computers writing, testing and designing code, which is one of the fastest-advancing areas for AI. India's IT services industry, with much of its work in maintenance, testing and outsourced development, is especially open to AI-driven productivity gains and restructuring.

title: Hairdressers, Beauticians and Related Workers
exposure_rationale: Cutting hair, shaving, facials and make-up are hands-on personal services, mostly delivered by self-employed barbers and beauticians in India. AI can at most help with booking or style suggestions; the core work is untouched.

title: Sheet and Structural Metal Workers, Moulders and Welders, and Related Workers
exposure_rationale: Welders, sheet metal workers, moulders, riggers and structural metal erectors do physical fabrication and erection work in workshops and on sites. AI has minimal effect on the core skills involved.

title: Subsistence Mixed Crop and Livestock Farmers
exposure_rationale: Subsistence mixed farmers combine crop growing and animal rearing for household consumption. The work is manual and outdoor, and AI is limited to marginal advisory information.

title: Textile, Fur and Leather Products Machine Operators
exposure_rationale: Spinning, weaving, sewing-machine, dyeing and laundry machine operators tend textile and leather machinery by hand. The work is physical and repetitive, and AI barely affects it.

title: Finance Professionals
exposure_rationale: Accountants, financial analysts and advisors in India work mostly with ledgers, GST and tax filings, reconciliations and financial reports, which are highly digital and increasingly automated. Client relationships, audit judgement and regulatory accountability keep humans involved, but productivity gains could reduce the number of workers needed.

title: Keyboard Operators
exposure_rationale: Typists, word processing operators and data entry clerks input and format text and data, which is routine and fully digital. OCR, speech recognition and AI document processing can already do most of this work today.

title: Refuse Workers
exposure_rationale: Garbage collectors, waste sorters and sweepers do manual sanitation work. AI has essentially no role in their daily tasks.

title: Nursing and Midwifery Associate Professionals
exposure_rationale: Nursing and midwifery associates (auxiliary nurses, ANMs) provide basic hands-on care, vaccinations, maternal care and patient support, often in public health settings. AI may help with records and reporting, but the core work is physical care and human contact.

title: Mining, Manufacturing and Construction Supervisors
exposure_rationale: Mining, manufacturing and construction supervisors spend most of their time on site directing workers, checking quality and enforcing safety. AI may help with scheduling, progress reports and material tracking, but the core of the job is physical, real-time supervision.

title: Other Clerical Support Workers
exposure_rationale: The group mixes highly exposed desk tasks (filing, coding, proof-reading, personnel records, correspondence) with physical roles that dominate Indian employment, such as postmen, office peons, daftries, process servers and patwaris doing field work. AI can sharply shrink the paper-processing share, but delivery, errand-running and in-person field duties are largely untouched.

title: Other Teaching Professionals
exposure_rationale: This group is dominated by private tutors, plus language, music, art and IT trainers, mostly self-employed and informal. Academic tuition and language and IT training face direct substitution from AI tutors, while music, dance and art teaching and special-needs teaching rely more on in-person demonstration and care.

title: Sales and Purchasing Agents and Brokers
exposure_rationale: Insurance agents, commercial sales representatives, buyers and trade brokers in India rely heavily on personal networks, door-to-door selling and negotiation, and 58% are self-employed. AI can generate leads, quotes and paperwork and online platforms disintermediate some sales, but trust-based relationship selling remains the core.

title: Business Services and Administration Managers
exposure_rationale: Finance, HR, policy and administration managers work mainly with reports, budgets, spreadsheets and communication, where AI tools already add a lot of productivity. Accountability, people management and organisational judgement keep humans in charge, but fewer managers and analysts may be needed for the same output.

title: Social and Religious Professionals
exposure_rationale: In India this group is dominated by religious professionals such as priests and preachers (66% self-employed, median education Class 10), whose work is ritual, ceremonial and community-based. Economists, psychologists and social scientists in the group are highly exposed, but they are a small share of workers.

title: Building and Housekeeping Supervisors
exposure_rationale: Housekeeping supervisors, caretakers and domestic housekeepers organize and carry out cleaning and upkeep of physical premises, and in India many also perform the work themselves. AI can help with scheduling, rostering and inventory of supplies, but supervising staff and maintaining buildings requires presence on site.

title: Fishery Workers, Hunters and Trappers
exposure_rationale: Fishers and aquaculture workers in India are mostly self-employed, working boats, nets and ponds by hand. AI-based fish-finding or weather advisories are marginal aids; the core work is physical.

title: Wood Treaters, Cabinet-makers and Related Trades Workers
exposure_rationale: Cabinet makers, wood treaters and woodworking machine operators build furniture and wood products by hand and machine. AI might assist with design, but the core work is physical craftsmanship.

title: Street Vendors (excluding Food)
exposure_rationale: Non-food street vendors and hawkers are almost all self-employed, with low education, selling goods door to door or along streets. The work is physical and face-to-face, with no meaningful AI impact.

title: Mobile Plant Operators
exposure_rationale: Tractor, excavator, crane and forklift operators control heavy machinery on farms, sites and warehouses. The work is physical and situational; AI has minimal effect.

title: Engineering Professionals (excluding Electro technology)
exposure_rationale: Civil, mechanical, chemical and industrial engineers do design, calculations, drawings, estimates and documentation that AI and generative design tools can increasingly handle. In India a large share work on construction sites and in plants, so site supervision, inspection and coordination keep a substantial physical component.

title: Other Elementary Workers
exposure_rationale: Messengers, delivery workers, porters, meter readers, ushers and odd-job workers do physical errands and on-site tasks. Smart meters and app-based dispatch erode a few roles, but the work remains largely manual.

title: Sales, Marketing and Development Managers
exposure_rationale: Sales, marketing and R&D managers plan campaigns, analyse market data, write proposals and manage teams, all mostly digital knowledge work that AI speeds up considerably. Relationship-heavy sales leadership and team management in Indian banks and trading firms add some protection, keeping this below the most exposed tier.

title: Other Stationary Plant and Machine Operators
exposure_rationale: Glass and ceramics plant operators, boiler operators, packing and bottling machine operators and gem machine operators tend physical production equipment. AI has minimal effect on their core tasks.

title: Tellers, Money Collectors and Related Clerks
exposure_rationale: Bank tellers handle cash, deposits and customer transactions, a role already shrinking with UPI, digital banking and ATMs, and the processing part is highly automatable. However, cash handling at counters and field debt collection and money-lending in India remain physical and relationship-based, keeping exposure from being very high.

title: Food and Related Products Machine Operators
exposure_rationale: Food machine operators run equipment for milling, processing and packaging food, often in small units. The work is physical machine tending with little AI involvement.

title: Sales, Marketing and Public Relations Professionals
exposure_rationale: Advertising, marketing and PR professionals do highly AI-exposed work like copywriting, campaign analysis and content creation. But in India a large share of this group are technical and medical sales representatives doing field visits to doctors, dealers and clients, where relationships and physical presence matter, which pulls the average down.

title: Electronics and Telecommunication Installers and Repairers
exposure_rationale: Electronics, mobile-phone and ICT equipment repairers and installers work hands-on with devices, cabling and network hardware, about half self-employed in India. AI can assist diagnosis and configuration, but repair and installation remain physical.

title: University and Higher Education Teachers
exposure_rationale: University teachers prepare lectures, grade work, conduct research and write papers, all knowledge work where AI is already very useful. In-person teaching, mentoring and lab supervision remain, but AI can substantially raise productivity in both teaching and research.

title: Numerical Clerks
exposure_rationale: Computing, posting and verifying accounting, payroll and statistical data is routine digital information processing that AI and modern accounting software already handle well. In India the work is mostly salaried, graduate-held and concentrated in banking and accounting firms, so it sits squarely in the path of automation; only the counter and cash-handling duties of bank clerks require physical presence.

title: Legal Professionals
exposure_rationale: Legal research and drafting petitions, contracts and opinions are text-heavy tasks where AI is advancing rapidly. Indian lawyers are mostly self-employed and spend much time on court appearances, client meetings and procedural work in physical courts, and judges carry decision-making authority, which tempers the exposure.

title: Artistic, Cultural and Culinary Associate Professionals
exposure_rationale: Despite the page title, this group's occupation families are photographers, interior decorators, chefs, tattoo artists, florists and other artistic and cultural associates, many self-employed or casual. Generative AI affects photography and interior design concept work, but most of the work, such as cooking, decorating, event setup and on-location shooting, is physical.

title: Manufacturing, Mining, Construction and Distribution Managers
exposure_rationale: Factory, construction, mining and logistics managers combine planning, scheduling, procurement and reporting (highly AI-assistable) with on-site supervision of workers, safety and physical operations. In India much of this work happens on construction sites and shop floors, so a substantial share still requires physical presence.

title: Vehicle, Window, Laundry and Other Hand Cleaning Workers
exposure_rationale: Hand launderers, ironing workers, vehicle washers and window cleaners do purely manual work, mostly self-employed. AI does not touch the job.

title: Waiters and Bartenders
exposure_rationale: Waiters and bartenders physically serve food and drinks and interact with customers in person. QR-code ordering and app-based billing take over small parts of order-taking, but the job remains overwhelmingly physical and interpersonal, especially in India's largely informal, casual-wage food service sector.

title: Retail and Wholesale Trade Managers
exposure_rationale: Most retail and wholesale trade managers in India are self-employed shop owners (71%) who handle stock, customers, credit and suppliers in person. AI can assist with inventory, ordering and digital catalogues, and e-commerce competition is a pressure, but daily work remains largely physical and relational.

title: Business Service Agents
exposure_rationale: Real estate brokers, clearing and forwarding agents, employment contractors and event planners in India are mostly self-employed intermediaries working through relationships and local knowledge. Documentation, listings and customs paperwork are increasingly digital and AI-assistable, while site visits, negotiation and arranging labour remain physical and interpersonal.

title: Medical Doctors
exposure_rationale: Doctors' diagnostic reasoning, documentation, imaging interpretation and treatment planning are areas where AI is making rapid progress. But Indian doctors, nearly half self-employed and seeing high patient volumes, spend most of their time on physical examination, procedures and in-person consultations, and they carry legal responsibility, which keeps the core human.

title: Blacksmiths, Tool Makers and Related Trades Workers
exposure_rationale: Blacksmiths, tool makers, machine tool setters and grinders shape and finish metal by hand and with machines. CNC programming and AI-assisted process optimisation touch the machine-setting side, but the work is predominantly hands-on in small Indian workshops.

title: Child Care Workers and Teachers' Aides
exposure_rationale: Child care workers, ayahs and teachers' aides, over half employed by the public sector in India, supervise, feed and care for young children in person. AI might help with record-keeping or activity ideas, but the core work of physical care and supervision is not touched.

title: Food Preparation Assistants
exposure_rationale: Fast-food preparers and kitchen helpers chop, wash, assemble and serve food in kitchens. The work is manual and AI has essentially no role in it.

title: Nursing and Midwifery Professionals
exposure_rationale: Nurses and midwives deliver hands-on patient care, medication administration, monitoring and childbirth support that require physical presence. AI can assist with charting, triage and care planning, but in India's stretched hospitals the core work is physical and interpersonal.

title: Forestry and Related Workers
exposure_rationale: Forestry workers plant, tend, fell and gather in forests, often as casual labour. The work is outdoor, physical and unpredictable, with essentially no AI involvement in daily tasks.

title: Rubber, Plastic and Paper Products Machine Operators
exposure_rationale: Rubber, plastic and paper products machine operators set up, feed and tend production machines on the shop floor. AI has little bearing on these physical machine-tending tasks.

title: Medical and Pharmaceutical Technicians
exposure_rationale: Medical imaging, lab and pharmacy technicians handle patients, samples and equipment in person. AI is advancing fast in image and lab result interpretation and pharmacy checks, but the practical tasks of positioning patients, drawing samples and dispensing remain physical.

title: Other Services Managers
exposure_rationale: This mixed group covers service managers in banking operations, warehousing, BPO, travel, sports and cultural centres. Scheduling, reporting and customer-contact management are increasingly AI-driven, but many of these roles involve running physical facilities and supervising staff on site.

title: Creative and Performing Artists
exposure_rationale: Indian creative and performing artists are mostly self-employed musicians, dancers, folk performers, actors and sculptors, many with low formal education. Live performance and hand-made art have natural barriers, though announcers, composers, digital visual artists and media directors face significant exposure from generative AI.

title: Professional Services Managers
exposure_rationale: Bank branch managers, hospital and school administrators and other service managers handle targets, compliance reporting, staff scheduling and customer escalations, much of it digital and AI-assistable. A large share of the job is supervising staff and dealing with customers, patients or parents in person, which keeps exposure in the high-moderate range.

title: Client Information Workers
exposure_rationale: Contact centre agents, receptionists, travel consultants and survey interviewers mostly provide and collect information by phone, chat or in person following scripts. AI voice and chat agents can already handle much of this, especially in India's large BPO sector, though front-desk receptionists in hospitals and hotels need some physical presence.

title: Chemical and Photographic Products Plant and Machine Operators
exposure_rationale: Chemical and photographic plant operators run and monitor mixing, reaction and processing equipment. AI-driven process control can assist with monitoring, but much of the work in Indian plants involves hands-on operation of machines and materials.

title: Travel Attendants, Conductors and Guides
exposure_rationale: Bus conductors, railway ticket examiners, guards, cabin crew and tour guides work in person, ensuring passenger safety, checking tickets and serving or escorting people. Digital ticketing and AI-powered travel information erode some ticketing and guiding tasks, but the core job requires physical presence on the vehicle or site.

title: Architects, Planners, Surveyors and Designers
exposure_rationale: This group mixes graphic and multimedia designers (very highly exposed), architects and product designers (substantially digital, with AI-assisted rendering and drafting) and surveyors and town planners with fieldwork. Overall the work product is mostly digital design, so exposure is high, with site visits, client relationships and survey fieldwork as partial barriers.

title: Administration Professionals
exposure_rationale: Management analysts, policy officers, HR and training professionals work largely on reports, analysis, policy documents and communications, which are core AI domains. Training delivery, stakeholder management and organisational politics add some interpersonal work, keeping this at high rather than very high exposure.

title: Other Health Professionals
exposure_rationale: Dentists, pharmacists, physiotherapists, optometrists and dieticians mostly provide hands-on or face-to-face services such as dental procedures, therapy sessions and dispensing in retail pharmacies. Some parts (nutrition plans, drug information checks, diagnostic reading) are AI-assistable, but most of the work requires physical presence.

title: Material Recording and Transport Clerks
exposure_rationale: Inventory, production-scheduling and transport-coordination records are information work that AI-driven inventory and logistics systems can largely absorb. In India, however, many of these workers are store keepers, stock verifiers and warehouse staff who physically receive, count, pick and dispatch goods, which keeps a substantial part of the job hands-on.

title: Government Regulatory Associate Professionals
exposure_rationale: Tax, customs, licensing and social benefit officials examine applications and documents, which is information processing that AI and e-governance can automate. However, this group also includes police inspectors, detectives and border inspectors whose field investigations and enforcement require physical presence and authority.

title: Physical and Engineering Science Technicians
exposure_rationale: Engineering technicians and draughtspersons combine computer work (CAD drafting, test analysis, documentation) that AI can automate with hands-on testing, inspection and maintenance in plants and utilities. In India many work in electricity and public works, keeping a significant physical component.

title: Financial and Mathematical Associate Professionals
exposure_rationale: Credit officers, accounting associates, statistical assistants, brokers and valuers process financial data, assess applications and execute transactions, mostly on computers. Credit decisions, bookkeeping and trading are already heavily automated and AI is advancing quickly, though some valuation and loss assessment needs site visits.

title: Information and Communication Technology Operations and User Support Technicians
exposure_rationale: ICT operations and user-support technicians monitor systems, troubleshoot user problems and maintain websites, largely through software. AI chatbots and automated IT operations can handle much tier-1 support, though hardware repairs and on-site support in Indian offices still need people.

title: Other Personal Services Workers
exposure_rationale: This group is unusually mixed: astrologers and fortune tellers deliver a conversational, information-based service that AI astrology apps are already imitating at scale, while pet groomers, undertakers and driving instructors do hands-on physical work. The blend yields moderate exposure, with the astrology segment far more exposed than the rest.

title: Assemblers
exposure_rationale: Assemblers put together mechanical and electronic components on factory lines. Robotics and AI-based visual inspection can automate parts of assembly and quality checks, but the core work is still manual.

title: Administrative and Specialized Secretaries
exposure_rationale: Administrative and executive secretaries and office supervisors handle correspondence, documents, scheduling and records, almost all of it digital. AI assistants can already draft, summarise and organise much of this work, though supervising clerks and acting as an organisational go-between need some human judgement.

title: Metal Processing and Finishing Plant Operators
exposure_rationale: Metal processing and plating operators run furnaces, rolling mills and finishing lines. Process-control and predictive-maintenance AI can optimise operations and reduce staffing at the margins, but operators still tend equipment physically.

title: Cashiers and Ticket Clerks
exposure_rationale: In India this group is dominated by graduate bank cashiers and railway or transport ticket clerks whose work is recording and processing payments and bookings on computers. UPI, online ticketing and AI-assisted self-service are already displacing much of the counter work, though cash handling and in-person customer service keep some presence requirement.

title: Hotel and Restaurant Managers
exposure_rationale: Hotel and restaurant managers in India, a large share of them owner-operators, spend most of their time on the floor supervising staff, handling guests, food quality and suppliers. AI can help with bookings, pricing, inventory and online reviews, but the hospitality core is physical and interpersonal.

title: Printing Trades Workers
exposure_rationale: Printing trades combine pre-press work (typesetting, layout, imaging) that is largely digital and exposed to AI design and layout tools with physical operation of presses, photocopiers and binding machines. Print demand is also being eroded by digital media, giving moderate exposure overall.

title: Process Control Technicians
exposure_rationale: Process control technicians operate and monitor power plants, water treatment and refinery control systems, where advanced automation and AI-based optimisation can reduce operator numbers. But plant rounds, manual interventions, maintenance and safety-critical response still require people on site.

title: Subsistence Fishers, Hunters, Trappers and Gatherers
exposure_rationale: Subsistence fishers, hunters, trappers and forest gatherers work physically in natural environments, and the median worker in India is not literate. AI has essentially no role in this work.

title: Legislators and Senior Officials
exposure_rationale: Senior officials spend much of their time on policy notes, file decisions, reviews and correspondence, all information work that AI can draft and summarise. But legislators, village heads and political office-bearers in India depend on constituency contact, negotiation and public accountability that stay with humans, so the job is reshaped rather than replaced.

title: Other Health Associate Professionals
exposure_rationale: This mixed group includes dental and physiotherapy assistants, ambulance workers and community health workers (mostly hands-on) along with medical records and health information technicians (highly exposed). Overall, physical and interpersonal care dominates, with AI affecting documentation and records.

title: Mining and Mineral Processing Plant Operators
exposure_rationale: Miners, quarriers, drillers and mineral-processing machine operators work in physical, hazardous environments, often as casual labour. AI-based process control is marginal to their daily work.

title: Street and Related Service Workers
exposure_rationale: Street service workers such as shoe-shiners and similar roadside service providers do manual work in public spaces. AI does not affect this work.

title: Information and Communications Technology Services Manager
exposure_rationale: ICT services managers oversee software development, IT infrastructure and telecom systems, working almost entirely on computers in domains where AI is advancing fastest. AI coding and operations tools directly restructure the teams they manage, and their own planning, vendor and reporting work is also highly automatable, though leadership and accountability remain human.

title: Personal Care Workers in Health Services
exposure_rationale: Health care assistants and home-based care workers help patients with mobility, bathing, feeding and daily living. This is hands-on, interpersonal care; AI can assist only with peripheral charting and scheduling.

title: Telecommunication and Broadcasting Technicians
exposure_rationale: Broadcasting and audio-visual technicians do recording, editing and transmission work that is increasingly automated and AI-assisted. Telecom technicians install and maintain towers, cables and equipment in the field, which is physical work, so overall exposure is moderate.

title: Other Craft and Related Workers
exposure_rationale: This mixed group includes divers, shot-firers and fumigators doing physical work, plus garment and product quality checkers and testers. Computer-vision inspection can automate parts of the grading and testing role, but most of the work remains hands-on.

title: Database and Network Professionals
exposure_rationale: Database administrators, system administrators and network professionals manage IT infrastructure that is largely configured and monitored through software, and AI-driven automation of operations and troubleshooting is advancing quickly. Some on-premises hardware and network work still requires physical presence.

title: Sports and Fitness Workers
exposure_rationale: Athletes, coaches, fitness instructors and sports officials do physical, in-person work. AI may help with training analytics and scheduling, but the core activity is physical performance and live instruction.

title: Paramedical Practitioners
exposure_rationale: Paramedical practitioners in India are often rural, self-employed providers giving injections, basic treatment and dispensing medicines in person. AI decision support could help with diagnosis, but the core of the work is hands-on care in low-resource settings with limited digital infrastructure.

title: Locomotive Engine Drivers and Related Workers
exposure_rationale: Locomotive drivers, brakers and signal and switch operators run trains and railway equipment. Automated signalling and train-control systems assist, but the work requires real-time physical presence and is little affected by AI in India.

title: Legal, Social and Religious Associate Professionals
exposure_rationale: This group combines paralegals and legal clerks (highly exposed document work) with social work associates doing community fieldwork and religious associates doing ritual work. In India a large self-employed and informal share is in community and religious roles, which keeps overall exposure moderate.

title: Electro-technology Engineers
exposure_rationale: Electrical, electronics and telecom engineers do circuit and system design, analysis and documentation that AI tools increasingly support. Many in India work in power utilities and equipment manufacturing, where commissioning, testing and maintaining physical systems on site remain central.

title: Wood Processing and Paper Making Plant Operators
exposure_rationale: Wood processing and paper-making plant operators run sawmills, veneer and pulp equipment, frequently as casual labour. AI does not meaningfully touch their daily physical work.

title: Authors, Journalists and Linguists
exposure_rationale: Authors, journalists, translators and interpreters produce written and spoken language, which is the core strength of modern AI. Machine translation and AI-generated content are already reshaping the field, though field reporting and live interpretation retain some human advantage.

title: Vocational Education Teachers
exposure_rationale: Vocational teachers in ITIs and training institutes teach practical trades and occupational skills, much of which involves hands-on demonstration and supervised practice. Lesson preparation, theory content and assessment are AI-assistable, giving a moderate exposure.

title: Secretaries (General)
exposure_rationale: General secretaries transcribe, format and check documents, manage correspondence and schedule appointments, nearly all routine digital tasks that AI assistants can already do. The remaining human element is mostly in-person coordination and handling visitors.

title: Traditional and Complementary Medicine Professionals
exposure_rationale: Ayurveda, homeopathy, Unani and similar practitioners consult with patients, examine them and prepare or dispense remedies, often in their own clinics. AI could help with information and record-keeping, but the practice rests on in-person consultation, trust and traditional hands-on methods.

title: Veterinarians
exposure_rationale: Veterinarians in India mostly treat livestock, often in rural areas (75% non-urban), involving physical examination, surgery, vaccination and artificial insemination. AI can help with diagnosis and records, but hands-on animal care dominates.

title: Veterinary Technicians and Assistants
exposure_rationale: Veterinary technicians and assistants handle, treat and care for animals, often livestock in rural settings, and assist with procedures. The work is almost entirely physical, with AI touching only record-keeping.

title: Production Managers in Agriculture, Forestry and Fisheries
exposure_rationale: Managers of plantations, farms, fisheries and cooperatives make planning, budgeting and record-keeping decisions that AI can support, for example with crop advisories and yield forecasting. Most of the work is directing labour, inspecting fields and stock, and handling weather and biological variability on site, which limits exposure.

title: Ships’ Deck Crews and Related Workers
exposure_rationale: Ships' deck crews and boatmen handle mooring, cargo and vessel upkeep, mostly self-employed in small craft in India. The work is physical and AI barely touches it.

title: Librarians, Archivists and Curators
exposure_rationale: Librarians, archivists and curators catalogue, classify and retrieve information, much of it increasingly digital and AI-assistable. Handling physical collections, preservation and serving users in person in educational institutions remain substantial parts of the job.

title: Physical and Earth Science Professionals
exposure_rationale: Chemists, physicists, geologists and meteorologists do analysis, modelling, literature work and report writing that AI accelerates strongly. In India many are chemists in pharmaceutical labs or field geologists, so hands-on experimentation, instruments and fieldwork still form a meaningful share of the job.

title: Traditional and Complementary Medicine Associate Professionals
exposure_rationale: Traditional medicine associates provide therapies such as Ayurvedic massage and herbal treatments and prepare remedies by hand. The work is hands-on and interpersonal, with only minor AI impact on paperwork and information.

title: Ship and Aircraft Controllers, and Technicians
exposure_rationale: Pilots, ships' officers and engineers, and air traffic controllers do safety-critical real-time work in physical vehicles and control towers. Autopilot, navigation and decision-support systems are increasingly capable, but regulation and the need for human command keep the core job human for now.

title: Life Science Technicians and Related Associate Professionals
exposure_rationale: Life science and agricultural technicians collect samples, run lab tests, maintain field trials and assist scientists, mostly hands-on. Data recording and analysis are AI-assistable, but the physical lab and field work dominates.

title: Life Science Professionals
exposure_rationale: Biologists, environmental professionals and farming/forestry advisors split their time between data analysis and writing (AI-exposed) and lab work, field surveys and farmer extension visits. The physical and interpersonal parts of the job, especially in agriculture extension, keep exposure moderate.

title: Mathematicians, Actuaries and Statisticians
exposure_rationale: Mathematicians, statisticians and actuaries work almost entirely on computers with data, models and written analysis. These are domains where AI is improving very rapidly, so the occupation faces major restructuring, with human judgement mainly in problem framing and sign-off.
